title: Review of ringswim c1 (SIMD): replicated on seed 6 with the mu=0 control; Supported, with a reticulate genealogy
summary: After the claim's sheets and strip_s1.png, I ran world_claim.py on seed 6 with labkit (200 frames x 50 steps = t 10000, because I left out the author's --spf 100) and with the author's celltrack.py to t=20000, and world_mu0.py with celltrack on seed 6. From noise, walled cells form by t~400, turn into crescents with depletion wakes and swim, often in loose chains, fusing and pinching (sheet t=2200-10000). celltrack: 40 track segments >= 3 body lengths (15 >= 5 BL; best 10.7 BL over 4640 t), 27 persistent splits, max generation 12, 68 splits vs 46 merges, 51 deaths; two cells were born by a split, swam 3.6 and 7.2 BL, and split again into two daughters (ids 152 and 109). mu=0 on the same seed: 29 persistent splits, generation 6, 0 merges, 0 segments >= 3 BL (best 1.7 BL). labkit on 10000 t: 0 persistent splits (merges 84 of 109 splits), L rim/core 1.43 (31/48 membrane-like).

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0: noise everywhere; cells by t=400
observations.I: rerun/sheet.png: discrete walled cells and crescents of bounded size t=400-10000
observations.M: celltrack_claim_s6.log: 40 segments >= 3 BL (15 >= 5 BL); celltrack_mu0_s6.log: 0 segments >= 3 BL with the drive off
observations.D: celltrack_claim_s6.log: 27 persistent splits, generation 12; cells 109 (7.2 BL) and 152 (3.6 BL) were born by a split, swam, and split into two surviving daughters

not_checked: labkit over the full t=20000 (my labkit run covers t=10000)
verdicts.limitation: Reticulate: merges are 68% of splits on seed 6, so confidence in D is capped at medium; labkit's own tracker (frames 50 t apart here) finds 0 persistent splits, and D rests on celltrack's 400 t hold rule. The drive is the per-body label-averaged gradient (nonlocal bookkeeping). No Laplacian-only twin.
